newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court rejects ban on Mitterrand aide's book.
newsitem.headline: French court rejects ban on Mitterrand aide's book.

text.p: A French court on Monday threw out a request that it ban a book by a member of the late President Francois Mitterrand's anti-terrorist unit which alleges a presidential aide was murdered in the presidential palace.
The Paris tribunal rejected an appeal made by Mitterrand's former adviser Michel Charasse following publication of "Secret Wars at the Elysee" by ex-police captain Paul Barril.

But it ordered the Albin Michel publishing house to put up a sign wherever the book, released on a first run of 85,000 copies, is on sale indicating that statements concerning Charasse are contested by him.
Gilles-Jean Portejoie, lawyer for former Socialist minister Charasse, said his client would sue Barril for libel and demand two million francs ($400,000) in damages.
The court is due to rule on another appeal for a ban filed by former Mitterrand chief of staff Gilles Menage.
"Gilles Menage and Michel Charasse are accused of ordering the murder of Francois de Grossouvre whereas the truth is he committed suicide at the Elysee (presidential palace," Portejoie said.
The book alleges that de Grossouvre, Mitterrand's old friend and confidant, found dead in 1994 in his Elysee office, did not commit suicide as officially reported but was murdered.

"The things in the book are common knowledge," Barril's lawyer Jacques Verges retorted at the hearing. "The aim is to muzzle the press without having a real debate. You are scared of suing us for libel," he said.
Barril says that Grossouvre was most likely murdered because he knew too much about corruption and other scandals undermining the Mitterrand administration.
